title: The role of the microbiome in pancreatic cancer personalized therapy prognosis
summary:
Pancreatic cancer has one of the poorest prognoses among all cancers. For pancreatic cancer patients, surgery unfortunately offers the only curative option, but this can only be offered in a small number of patients. Borderline inoperable tumors can become operable with prior (neoadjuvant) therapy in approximately 65% of cases. In directly operated pancreatic cancer patients with subsequent (adjuvant) therapy, tumor recurrence is very high relative to other cancers. Why some patients respond positively to neoadjuvant therapy and others do not, and why recurrence occurs earlier in some patients after adjuvant therapy than in others, is still completely unknown.
The intestinal flora with the different bacterial species can potentially influence tumorigenesis, therapy efficacy, and metastasis. The intestinal flora contains more microbes than the human body itself has cells. Initial results have shown that certain strains of bacteria are more likely to have a positive effect on cancer treatment and prognosis. Other intestinal bacteria strains have a negative effect. If it were possible to identify the most common intestinal bacterial species that have a positive effect on anti-cancer treatment, it would be possible to replace the negative bacterial strains via fecal transplantation. This could improve success rates in pancreatic cancer. First, the bacterial strains present in the intestine and also in the pancreas need to be determined and the bacteria with more favorable or unfavorable therapy prognosis identified. For this purpose, fecal samples from pancreatic cancer patients are collected before and after neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy, the bacterial DNA is extracted, and the bacterial species and quantity are determined via sequencing. Bacterial flora will also be collected in tumor tissue after each resection and the microbiome will be determined. These studies will select those bacterial strains that correlate with a more favorable prognosis. Subsequently, immunofluorescence in pancreatic cancer tissue will be used to examine the inflammatory signals emitted by the bacterial strains present in the intestine or pancreas. Favorable bacterial strains may promote tumor infiltrating immune cells with predominantly positive anti-tumor activity, while unfavorable bacterial strains may promote more tumor promoting infiltrating immune cells. Tissue studies can be used to determine the different bacterial species in the intestine or pancreatic tissue for their effect in pancreatic cancer. Fecal transplantation could replace unfavorable bacterial strains with more favorable bacteria and possibly increase therapy effectiveness.
conditions: Disorders of gallbladder, biliary tract and pancreas

interventions.name: Comparison of stool and tissue microbiomes of pancreatitis and IPMN patients (serving as tumor precursors with and increased tumor risk) with the stool and tissue microbiome of patients with pancreatic cancer.
From the collected stool and tissue samples, the microbiome is determined and with the prognosis correlated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pancreatic diseases (pancreatitis, IPMN, PDAC).
Exclusion criteria:
not pancreatic disease.
